question_text: According to the law of demand, what happens to the quantity demanded of a good when its price increases?
options: A) Quantity demanded increases
B) Quantity demanded decreases
C) Quantity demanded remains the same
D) Quantity demanded becomes unpredictable
explanation: The law of demand states that, all else being equal, the quantity demanded of a good decreases as its price increases, reflecting an inverse relationship. This is illustrated by a downward-sloping demand curve. (Source: doc7::concept::2::law_of_demand)

question_text: What does a demand curve typically show in a graph?
options: The relationship between price and quantity supplied
The relationship between price and quantity demanded
The total revenue of a firm at different prices
The cost of production at different output levels
correct_answer: The relationship between price and quantity demanded
explanation: A demand curve illustrates how the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing to buy changes as the price varies, with higher prices typically leading to lower quantities demanded. (Source: doc7::concept::6::demand_curve)

question_text: What is the relationship between price and quantity demanded, as illustrated by a downward-sloping demand curve?
options: A. Price and quantity demanded are directly related.
B. Price and quantity demanded are inversely related.
C. Price and quantity demanded are unrelated.
D. Quantity demanded determines the price.
explanation: The downward-sloping demand curve illustrates the law of demand, showing that as price decreases, quantity demanded increases, and vice versa. This inverse relationship is a fundamental concept in economics. (Source: doc7::concept::1::quantity_demanded)

question_text: According to the law of supply, what happens to the quantity supplied of a good when its price increases?
options: A) The quantity supplied decreases.
B) The quantity supplied increases.
C) The quantity supplied remains unchanged.
D) The quantity supplied becomes unpredictable.
explanation: The law of supply states that, all else being equal, an increase in the price of a good leads to an increase in the quantity supplied. This is represented by an upward-sloping supply curve (doc7::concept::5::law_of_supply).

question_text: Which of the following best describes the typical shape of a supply curve on a graph?
options: A downward-sloping line from left to right
A horizontal line parallel to the x-axis
An upward-sloping line from left to right
A vertical line parallel to the y-axis
correct_answer: An upward-sloping line from left to right
explanation: The supply curve is upward-sloping because, according to the law of supply, as the price of a good increases, the quantity supplied also increases, assuming all else is equal. This relationship is visually represented by an upward-sloping line on a graph with price on the y-axis and quantity supplied on the x-axis. (Source: doc7::chunk::14)
